close_reason: wontfix: bikeshedding. Epic JMAP-6r7c explicitly flagged this as 'pure forward-major-version flag or naming preference with no engineering pressure on the current 0.x crate. Filed for completeness, but a /do-beads pass that closes them as wontfix is the right outcome unless the workspace is planning the next major bump.' The doc-comment already states the unit ('Default: 1 MiB.'). Field names like max_call_body are conventional Rust idiom; bytes is the implicit unit for any 'size cap' field. If the workspace ever adopts a unit-in-name discipline workspace-wide, file a sweep bead at that time covering all *-server, *-client, and *-types crates rather than spot-fixing one struct in jmap-base-client.
description:
client.rs:43-80 — ClientConfig

Field names: max_session_body, max_call_body, max_download_body, max_upload_response_body, max_sse_frame, max_ws_message.

The doc-comments correctly state "Default: 1 MiB." etc. But the field names themselves do not include the unit. A caller reading:
  config.max_call_body = 8000000;

…cannot tell from the line alone whether that's 8 million bytes (probably right) or 8 million KiB (definitely wrong) or 8 million bits. The unit is in the doc-comment, but not at the field-access site.

Idiom in well-engineered Rust APIs: name the unit in the field — `max_call_body_bytes`, `max_sse_frame_bytes`, etc. This is the same reason std uses `Duration::from_millis()` not `Duration::from(1000)`.

This applies to the field naming choice on a public struct. Renaming the fields is a breaking change (callers using struct-literal `..ClientConfig::default()` are unaffected, but callers using `let body_cap = config.max_call_body;` would need to update). Pre-1.0 this is OK.

Same applies to `request_timeout: Duration` — the unit is implicit in the type, so this one is fine.

Recommendation: in next minor or major release, consider renaming to *_bytes consistently. Low priority because (a) all the docs already say "bytes", (b) the integer types are correct (u64 / usize), and (c) the workspace cookie-cutter rule keeps the names stable across sibling crates so a rename ripples — which is fine but the propagation cost should be planned.
title: ClientConfig fields max_session_body/max_call_body/etc lack stated unit in field name
